easy.question: What will the Israelites do after they inherit the land?
answers: Return to Egypt
Live in cities and houses
Build only tents
easy.explanation: The passage says they will inherit the land and live in cities and houses.

easy.question: How many cities does the Torah command them to set apart?
answers: Three
Two
Six
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “You shall separate three cities.”

easy.question: Who are the cities to be set apart for?
answers: Anyone who flees there after killing someone
The kings of the nations
The priests only
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says the road is to be prepared so that any killer may flee there.

medium.question: Why are they commanded to prepare the road to the cities?
answers: To expand the land
So the killer can reach a city quickly
To hide the cities
medium.explanation: The road is to be ready so the killer can flee to one of the cities of refuge.

medium.question: What does the phrase “prepare the way for yourself” mean here?
answers: Pave and arrange the road
Abandon the road
Forbid travel on the road
medium.explanation: In context, the road must be made ready so the killer can escape to the city.

medium.question: What does “divide the borders of your land into three parts” mean?
answers: Add three new countries
Surround the land with a wall
Divide the land into three regions
medium.explanation: The land is to be divided into three regions so the cities of refuge will be accessible.

challenge.question: What sequence of actions emerges from these verses?
answers: Prepare the road, conquer the land, then receive it
Receive and inherit the land, live in it, then set apart the cities and prepare the road
Set apart the cities, leave the land, then live in houses
challenge.explanation: First God gives the land and the people inherit and live in it; afterward they set apart the cities and prepare the road.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command to divide the land into three parts?
answers: The goal is for every place in the land to be relatively near a city of refuge
The goal is for every tribe to receive three cities
The goal is to eliminate tribal boundaries
challenge.explanation: Dividing the land into three parts spreads out the cities and makes them accessible from every region.

challenge.question: What does the transition from “which the Lord gives you” to “separate,” “prepare,” and “divide” emphasize?
answers: That the people need do nothing after receiving the land
That God gives the land, but the people must make practical preparations within it
That the people receive only the cities, not the land
challenge.explanation: The verses combine God’s gift of the land with the people’s responsibility to prepare the cities, roads, and boundaries.

questions.question: What sequence of actions emerges from these verses?
answers: Prepare the road, conquer the land, then receive it
Receive and inherit the land, live in it, then set apart the cities and prepare the road
Set apart the cities, leave the land, then live in houses
questions.explanation: First God gives the land and the people inherit and live in it; afterward they set apart the cities and prepare the road.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command to divide the land into three parts?
answers: The goal is for every place in the land to be relatively near a city of refuge
The goal is for every tribe to receive three cities
The goal is to eliminate tribal boundaries
questions.explanation: Dividing the land into three parts spreads out the cities and makes them accessible from every region.

questions.question: What does the transition from “which the Lord gives you” to “separate,” “prepare,” and “divide” emphasize?
answers: That the people need do nothing after receiving the land
That God gives the land, but the people must make practical preparations within it
That the people receive only the cities, not the land
questions.explanation: The verses combine God’s gift of the land with the people’s responsibility to prepare the cities, roads, and boundaries.

paragraphs.title: Accidental Killing and Fleeing to a City of Refuge

easy.question: Which killer must flee to a city of refuge?
answers: Someone who killed unintentionally
Someone who planned the killing
Someone who fled from the city
easy.explanation: The passage describes someone who struck his neighbor unintentionally.

easy.question: Where did the incident described in verse 5 take place?
answers: In a field
In a forest
In a city
easy.explanation: The man went with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood.

easy.question: What happened after the iron head slipped from the axe?
answers: The man fled immediately
The tree fell on the woodcutter
The iron struck his neighbor, and he died
easy.explanation: The iron slipped from the handle, struck his neighbor, and killed him.

medium.question: Why is the man described as an accidental killer rather than an intentional murderer?
answers: He struck without intending to, and he did not hate his neighbor
He was not in the forest
He intended to kill someone else
medium.explanation: The passage stresses that the blow was unintentional and that there had been no previous hatred.

medium.question: In the phrase “whom he hated not in time past,” what does “in time past” mean?
answers: In the distant forest
Previously or formerly
After the incident
medium.explanation: The phrase means that he had not hated his neighbor beforehand.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the woodcutting example?
answers: The iron slipped, the man entered the forest, and then he began chopping
The man killed intentionally, fled, and afterward entered the forest
The man entered the forest, began chopping, and the iron slipped and struck his neighbor
medium.explanation: The verse describes entering the forest, chopping wood, the iron slipping, and striking the neighbor.

challenge.question: Which detail especially distinguishes accidental killing from killing out of hatred?
answers: That the event happened in a forest
That he had not hated his neighbor beforehand
That the man was holding an axe
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says there had been no previous hatred, presenting the death as an accident rather than revenge.

challenge.question: Why does the Torah give the example of an axe head slipping while wood is being cut?
answers: To teach that every woodcutter is a murderer
To show how an ordinary activity can unintentionally cause death
To forbid entering forests
challenge.explanation: The example shows that death can occur during ordinary work without planning or hatred.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated idea that the person may “live”?
answers: The killer must remain in the forest
The dead person will return to life
The city of refuge protects the accidental killer from danger
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the person who flees to the city can be saved and remain alive.

questions.question: Which detail especially distinguishes accidental killing from killing out of hatred?
answers: That the event happened in a forest
That he had not hated his neighbor beforehand
That the man was holding an axe
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says there had been no previous hatred, presenting the death as an accident rather than revenge.

questions.question: Why does the Torah give the example of an axe head slipping while wood is being cut?
answers: To teach that every woodcutter is a murderer
To show how an ordinary activity can unintentionally cause death
To forbid entering forests
questions.explanation: The example shows that death can occur during ordinary work without planning or hatred.

questions.question: What can be understood from the repeated idea that the person may “live”?
answers: The killer must remain in the forest
The dead person will return to life
The city of refuge protects the accidental killer from danger
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the person who flees to the city can be saved and remain alive.

paragraphs.title: Protection from the Avenger of Blood

easy.question: What does Moses command them to set apart?
answers: Three cities
Three families
Three judges
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “You shall separate three cities.”

easy.question: Who might pursue the killer?
answers: The king
The avenger of blood
The priest
easy.explanation: The verse warns that the avenger of blood might pursue the killer.

easy.question: Why is the killer not subject to death in the case described?
answers: Because he was young
Because he fled the city
Because he had not hated the person who died
easy.explanation: The passage explains that he had not hated the victim beforehand.

medium.question: What could happen if the road were too long?
answers: The avenger of blood might overtake and kill the killer
The killer would return home
The people would abolish the cities
medium.explanation: If the way were too long, the avenger might overtake and kill him.

medium.question: What does “avenger of blood” mean in this context?
answers: Someone who tries to save the killer
A relative seeking to avenge the victim’s blood
A judge who decides the case
medium.explanation: The context describes a relative pursuing the killer to avenge the victim.

medium.question: What is the connection between setting apart the cities and the danger described?
answers: The cities were meant to remove the killer from the land
The cities allowed the killer to escape punishment forever
The cities provided a nearby, safe place until the case could be judged
medium.explanation: The cities prevented the avenger from overtaking the accidental killer before the case was decided.

challenge.question: Which phrase proves that the killing did not arise from previous hatred?
answers: “In time past”
“If the way be long”
“Three cities”
challenge.explanation: “In time past” emphasizes that the killer had not previously hated the victim.

challenge.question: Why does the Torah emphasize that the avenger’s heart may be hot?
answers: To explain why he might act quickly and angrily before the case was judged
To teach that the avenger must be a leader
To show that the killer intended to kill
challenge.explanation: A hot heart explains the danger of an angry, immediate response that could kill someone who did not deserve death.

challenge.question: What principle emerges from the movement between verses 6 and 7?
answers: Family revenge is more important than justice
Immediate revenge must be prevented when the killing may have been unintentional
Every killing requires fleeing to another city
challenge.explanation: The cities protect an accidental killer until the facts and the law can be considered, rather than allowing immediate revenge.

questions.question: Which phrase proves that the killing did not arise from previous hatred?
answers: “In time past”
“If the way be long”
“Three cities”
questions.explanation: “In time past” emphasizes that the killer had not previously hated the victim.

questions.question: Why does the Torah emphasize that the avenger’s heart may be hot?
answers: To explain why he might act quickly and angrily before the case was judged
To teach that the avenger must be a leader
To show that the killer intended to kill
questions.explanation: A hot heart explains the danger of an angry, immediate response that could kill someone who did not deserve death.

questions.question: What principle emerges from the movement between verses 6 and 7?
answers: Family revenge is more important than justice
Immediate revenge must be prevented when the killing may have been unintentional
Every killing requires fleeing to another city
questions.explanation: The cities protect an accidental killer until the facts and the law can be considered, rather than allowing immediate revenge.

paragraphs.title: Adding Cities of Refuge and Preventing the Shedding of Innocent Blood

easy.question: What does the Lord promise to do to Israel’s borders?
answers: Enlarge them
Reduce them
Remove them
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “If the Lord your God enlarge your borders.”

easy.question: How many additional cities are to be added?
answers: One city
Three cities
Six cities
easy.explanation: Verse 9 commands them to add three more cities to the original three.

easy.question: What are they to prevent, according to verse 10?
answers: The loss of the land
The shedding of innocent blood
The enlargement of the borders
easy.explanation: The verse warns against shedding innocent blood in the land.

medium.question: On what condition would Israel add three more cities?
answers: If they kept the commandments, loved the Lord, and walked in His ways
If they built walls around every city
If they conquered new countries
medium.explanation: The additional cities are connected with keeping the commandments, loving the Lord, and walking in His ways.

medium.question: What does “inheritance” mean in the phrase “the land which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance”?
answers: Land or a portion of land given to a person or people
A punishment for sin
A road for traveling
medium.explanation: Here, “inheritance” means the land that the Lord gives Israel as a possession.

medium.question: Why is keeping the commandments connected with preventing the shedding of innocent blood?
answers: Because obedience requires responsibility and justice in the land
Because the commandments eliminate the need for cities
Because obedience prevents the borders from expanding
medium.explanation: The verses present obedience as a condition for a just society in which innocent blood is not shed.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “three more cities beside these three”?
answers: There were already three cities, so the total would be six
The first three cities were canceled
The total would remain three
challenge.explanation: “Three more” means three are added to the original three, making six altogether.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the expansion of the land and the addition of cities of refuge?
answers: As the land expands, more cities are needed to protect people and reduce the shedding of innocent blood
The expansion of the land eliminates the need for cities of refuge
The cities were meant only to mark the borders
challenge.explanation: When the territory grows, additional cities help protect those who need refuge and prevent innocent bloodshed.

challenge.question: What does “blood will be upon you” teach about the people’s responsibility?
answers: The people are responsible only for collecting taxes
The people are not responsible for bloodshed
The people may bear guilt if they fail to prevent the shedding of innocent blood
challenge.explanation: The phrase warns that the people will be held responsible if innocent blood is not prevented.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “three more cities beside these three”?
answers: There were already three cities, so the total would be six
The first three cities were canceled
The total would remain three
questions.explanation: “Three more” means three are added to the original three, making six altogether.

questions.question: What is the connection between the expansion of the land and the addition of cities of refuge?
answers: As the land expands, more cities are needed to protect people and reduce the shedding of innocent blood
The expansion of the land eliminates the need for cities of refuge
The cities were meant only to mark the borders
questions.explanation: When the territory grows, additional cities help protect those who need refuge and prevent innocent bloodshed.

questions.question: What does “blood will be upon you” teach about the people’s responsibility?
answers: The people are responsible only for collecting taxes
The people are not responsible for bloodshed
The people may bear guilt if they fail to prevent the shedding of innocent blood
questions.explanation: The phrase warns that the people will be held responsible if innocent blood is not prevented.

paragraphs.title: The Intentional Murderer and His Punishment

easy.question: What did the man do to his neighbor?
answers: He killed him
He rescued him
He invited him into his home
easy.explanation: The man lay in wait, struck his neighbor, and killed him.

easy.question: Where did the man flee after killing his neighbor?
answers: To his home
To one of the cities of refuge
To another country
easy.explanation: The verse says he fled to one of the designated cities.

easy.question: What were they commanded not to do to the murderer?
answers: Speak to him
Take his possessions
Pity him
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Your eye shall not pity him.”

medium.question: Why did the elders of the murderer’s city take him out of the city?
answers: To hand him over to the avenger of blood
To protect him
To send him into exile
medium.explanation: The elders were to bring him out and deliver him to the avenger of blood.

medium.question: What does “into the hand of the avenger of blood” mean?
answers: Into the hands of the person who avenges the victim’s blood
Into the hands of someone who cleans the blood
Into the hands of someone who treats the wounded
medium.explanation: The murderer is handed over to the person responsible for avenging the victim.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Killing, fleeing to a city, and being handed over to the avenger of blood
Fleeing, reconciliation, and returning home
A trial, imprisonment, and flight from the land
medium.explanation: First the man kills, then flees to a city, and finally the elders hand him over.

challenge.question: Why does fleeing to a city of refuge not protect him in this case?
answers: He killed intentionally after hating and ambushing his neighbor
The city was too far away
He could not find the city gate
challenge.explanation: The passage describes hatred, an ambush, and an intentional attack—not accidental killing.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “innocent blood” refer to?
answers: The murderer’s blood
The blood of the innocent person who was killed
Blood shed in the city of refuge
challenge.explanation: The blood is called innocent because the victim did not deserve to die.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command “that it may go well with you” after requiring the murderer’s punishment?
answers: The punishment is only for personal revenge
The punishment guarantees that the murderer can escape
Punishing the murderer preserves the community’s purity and removes bloodguilt
challenge.explanation: The conclusion teaches that removing innocent-blood guilt benefits the entire community.

questions.question: Why does fleeing to a city of refuge not protect him in this case?
answers: He killed intentionally after hating and ambushing his neighbor
The city was too far away
He could not find the city gate
questions.explanation: The passage describes hatred, an ambush, and an intentional attack—not accidental killing.

questions.question: What does the phrase “innocent blood” refer to?
answers: The murderer’s blood
The blood of the innocent person who was killed
Blood shed in the city of refuge
questions.explanation: The blood is called innocent because the victim did not deserve to die.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command “that it may go well with you” after requiring the murderer’s punishment?
answers: The punishment is only for personal revenge
The punishment guarantees that the murderer can escape
Punishing the murderer preserves the community’s purity and removes bloodguilt
questions.explanation: The conclusion teaches that removing innocent-blood guilt benefits the entire community.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition Against Moving a Boundary Marker

easy.question: What is forbidden according to the verse?
answers: Moving your neighbor’s boundary marker
Building a tall house
Moving to another city
easy.explanation: The verse forbids moving the boundary marker belonging to a neighbor.

easy.question: Who established the boundaries mentioned in the verse?
answers: The kings
Those who lived before
The merchants
easy.explanation: The boundaries were set by people in earlier generations.

easy.question: Who gives Israel the land, according to the verse?
answers: The elders
The neighbors
The Lord your God
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord your God gives Israel the land to possess.

medium.question: Why is it forbidden to move your neighbor’s boundary?
answers: To preserve the division of inheritances that was established
So everyone will move to one city
To increase the size of the country
medium.explanation: The prohibition protects the boundaries and inheritances established in the past.

medium.question: What does “move” mean in “you shall not move your neighbor’s landmark”?
answers: Praise
Shift or push back
Protect
medium.explanation: In this context, it means moving the boundary from its place and reducing your neighbor’s land.

medium.question: What is the relationship between an inheritance and a boundary in the verse?
answers: The boundary determines the area of each person’s inheritance
The boundary prevents anyone from receiving an inheritance
The inheritance is located only outside the land
medium.explanation: Boundaries divide the land into inheritances, so moving one harms another person’s inheritance.

challenge.question: Which important detail is easy to miss in the wording of the prohibition?
answers: It concerns only city boundaries
It applies only to new boundaries
It forbids moving your neighbor’s boundary
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes your neighbor’s boundary, meaning that no part of another person’s inheritance may be taken.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “which those of old time have set”?
answers: A division established by earlier generations should be respected
Every old boundary may be canceled
Earlier generations did not know how to divide the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase teaches that boundaries established in the past are binding and should be honored.

challenge.question: How does the verse present the relationship between human ownership of the land and God?
answers: People received the land entirely independently of God
God gives the land, so it must be treated honestly
The land belongs only to neighbors
challenge.explanation: Because God gives the land, its divisions and the treatment of others’ property must be handled responsibly and fairly.

questions.question: Which important detail is easy to miss in the wording of the prohibition?
answers: It concerns only city boundaries
It applies only to new boundaries
It forbids moving your neighbor’s boundary
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes your neighbor’s boundary, meaning that no part of another person’s inheritance may be taken.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “which those of old time have set”?
answers: A division established by earlier generations should be respected
Every old boundary may be canceled
Earlier generations did not know how to divide the land
questions.explanation: The phrase teaches that boundaries established in the past are binding and should be honored.

questions.question: How does the verse present the relationship between human ownership of the land and God?
answers: People received the land entirely independently of God
God gives the land, so it must be treated honestly
The land belongs only to neighbors
questions.explanation: Because God gives the land, its divisions and the treatment of others’ property must be handled responsibly and fairly.

paragraphs.title: The Need for Two or Three Witnesses

easy.question: What is not enough to establish a person’s guilt or sin?
answers: One witness
Two witnesses
Three witnesses
easy.explanation: The verse says that one witness shall not be sufficient.

easy.question: On the testimony of how many witnesses may a matter be established?
answers: One witness only
Two or three witnesses
Exactly four witnesses
easy.explanation: The verse says that the matter is established by two or three witnesses.

easy.question: What does “in any sin that he sins” refer to?
answers: Only a minor sin
Only an offense before a court
Any sin that a person commits
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the rule applies to every sin a person commits.

medium.question: What is the result of having only one witness?
answers: The testimony is not enough to establish the matter
It is always sufficient
It is sufficient only if the witness is elderly
medium.explanation: One witness alone cannot establish a person’s guilt.

medium.question: What condition allows a matter to be established?
answers: The accused must confess immediately
There must be testimony from two or three witnesses
The act must be especially serious
medium.explanation: The verse connects establishing the matter with the testimony of two or three witnesses.

medium.question: In the verse, what does “established” mean?
answers: Standing in one place
Going to court
Being accepted as sufficient proof of the matter
medium.explanation: In a legal context, it means that the testimony is accepted as sufficient to establish the matter.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both two and three witnesses?
answers: There must always be three witnesses
Two witnesses can be sufficient, and three are also possible
There may never be more than two witnesses
challenge.explanation: The verse says “by two witnesses or by three,” so two are sufficient and three are also permitted.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “at the mouth of” emphasize?
answers: That the decision is based on the witnesses’ testimony
That the witnesses must speak at the same time
That the accused may choose the witnesses
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the matter is established according to the testimony of two or three witnesses.

challenge.question: Which statement fits the broad rule in this verse?
answers: The rule applies only to secret sins
The rule applies only when there are three witnesses
The rule applies to every iniquity and sin, not just one type
challenge.explanation: The verse repeatedly broadens the rule to every kind of iniquity and sin.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both two and three witnesses?
answers: There must always be three witnesses
Two witnesses can be sufficient, and three are also possible
There may never be more than two witnesses
questions.explanation: The verse says “by two witnesses or by three,” so two are sufficient and three are also permitted.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “at the mouth of” emphasize?
answers: That the decision is based on the witnesses’ testimony
That the witnesses must speak at the same time
That the accused may choose the witnesses
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the matter is established according to the testimony of two or three witnesses.

questions.question: Which statement fits the broad rule in this verse?
answers: The rule applies only to secret sins
The rule applies only when there are three witnesses
The rule applies to every iniquity and sin, not just one type
questions.explanation: The verse repeatedly broadens the rule to every kind of iniquity and sin.

easy.question: Who rises against a person to give false testimony?
answers: A false witness
A priest
A judge
easy.explanation: The verse begins by describing a false witness who rises against a person.

easy.question: Before whom do the two people in a dispute stand?
answers: Before the king alone
Before the Lord, the priests, and the judges
Before all the people
easy.explanation: The verse says they stand before the Lord and before the priests and judges.

easy.question: What do the judges do in this case?
answers: Believe the witness immediately
Punish both people
Make a careful investigation
easy.explanation: The judges are commanded to inquire carefully.

medium.question: Why must the judges investigate carefully?
answers: To determine whether the testimony is true or false
To choose a new priest
To finish the hearing quickly
medium.explanation: The investigation is intended to discover whether the witness is truthful.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events described in these verses?
answers: The judges punish first, and then the witness arrives
A witness testifies, the disputing parties stand before the authorities, and the judges investigate
The priests testify, and then the people investigate
medium.explanation: First a person is accused, then the parties appear before the authorities, and finally the judges investigate.

medium.question: In the phrase “to testify against him that which is wrong,” what does “wrong” mean?
answers: A short answer
A false or harmful accusation
Praise for the person
medium.explanation: Here it refers to an evil or false accusation made against the person.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the judges’ not accepting the witness’s testimony immediately?
answers: Every testimony must be examined before judgment is given
Witnesses may not testify in court
Only priests may investigate
challenge.explanation: The command to investigate carefully teaches that testimony must be examined before a decision is made.

challenge.question: Who are “the two men between whom the controversy is”?
answers: Two priests
The two parties involved in the dispute
The witness and the judge
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the two people involved in the legal dispute.

challenge.question: What does the repeated conclusion “the witness is a false witness” emphasize?
answers: That there were two different witnesses
That the judges did not hear the testimony
That the investigation established that the witness lied
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the result of the investigation: the witness was proven false.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the judges’ not accepting the witness’s testimony immediately?
answers: Every testimony must be examined before judgment is given
Witnesses may not testify in court
Only priests may investigate
questions.explanation: The command to investigate carefully teaches that testimony must be examined before a decision is made.

questions.question: Who are “the two men between whom the controversy is”?
answers: Two priests
The two parties involved in the dispute
The witness and the judge
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the two people involved in the legal dispute.

questions.question: What does the repeated conclusion “the witness is a false witness” emphasize?
answers: That there were two different witnesses
That the judges did not hear the testimony
That the investigation established that the witness lied
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the result of the investigation: the witness was proven false.

paragraphs.title: Punishment for a False Witness and Deterring Evil

easy.question: What must be done to someone who plotted to harm his fellow?
answers: Do to him what he plotted to do
Forgive him immediately
Send him somewhere else
easy.explanation: The verse commands that he be treated as he intended to treat his fellow.

easy.question: What will the punishment and judgment cause other people to do?
answers: Forget the incident
Hear and be afraid
Leave the land
easy.explanation: The verse says that others will hear and fear, so they will not commit similar evil.

easy.question: What is the person carrying out the judgment told?
answers: Always to pity the wrongdoer
To ignore the act
Not to let his eye show pity
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Your eye shall not pity.”

medium.question: How does the punishment help stop evil acts?
answers: It also deters others from doing evil
It only removes the injured person
It ends the hearing of witnesses
medium.explanation: The verses say that others will hear and fear and will not commit similar evil.

medium.question: What does “plotted” mean in “as he had thought to have done to his brother”?
answers: Forgot
Planned or intended
Asked forgiveness
medium.explanation: The word means that he planned or intended to do the evil act.

medium.question: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?
answers: First fear, then planning, and finally hearing
First forgiveness, then flight, and finally judgment
First carrying out the judgment, then deterring others, and finally explaining the principle of matching punishment
medium.explanation: The passage first describes the judgment, then its deterrent purpose, and finally the principle of equal punishment.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “those who remain”?
answers: They are only the wrongdoer’s relatives
They are people who can still hear and learn from the judgment
They are people who fled the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to others who can hear the judgment and be warned by it.

challenge.question: What does the list “life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot” teach?
answers: The judgment should correspond to the type of injury
Every injury must always receive exactly the same punishment
The verse concerns only injuries to the feet
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that the punishment should correspond to the life or body part affected.

challenge.question: Why is “your eye shall not pity” emphasized after the command to punish?
answers: So the judgment will be carried out secretly
To prevent personal sympathy from canceling justice and deterrence
To require the injured person to take revenge personally
challenge.explanation: The judge must not allow personal pity to prevent justice, since the judgment also removes evil and deters others.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “those who remain”?
answers: They are only the wrongdoer’s relatives
They are people who can still hear and learn from the judgment
They are people who fled the land
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to others who can hear the judgment and be warned by it.

questions.question: What does the list “life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot” teach?
answers: The judgment should correspond to the type of injury
Every injury must always receive exactly the same punishment
The verse concerns only injuries to the feet
questions.explanation: The list emphasizes that the punishment should correspond to the life or body part affected.

questions.question: Why is “your eye shall not pity” emphasized after the command to punish?
answers: So the judgment will be carried out secretly
To prevent personal sympathy from canceling justice and deterrence
To require the injured person to take revenge personally
questions.explanation: The judge must not allow personal pity to prevent justice, since the judgment also removes evil and deters others.
